---

1/ Added a --dry-run flag to my CLI tool on a whim. Three months later, I've used it almost every single day.

2/ You know that tiny pause before hitting Enter on a destructive command? That "wait... did I check the path?" moment?

3/ --dry-run kills that anxiety. Shows exactly what would happen, without actually doing it. I run it reflexively now, no second-guessing.

4/ What surprised me: I use it more for confidence than debugging. Just a quick "yep, everything looks right" before starting work. Config loaded? State makes sense? Good to go.

5/ The implementation? Maybe 5-10 if (dryRun) checks scattered through the codebase. The payoff? I move faster because I'm not constantly triple-checking before execution.

6/ Not every tool needs this. But CLIs that create/modify/delete things? It's the kind of small feature that removes way more friction than you'd expect.

7/ The best dev tools aren't always clever algorithms. Sometimes they're just thoughtful guardrails that let you move fast without fear of breaking everything.
